Dichotomous key

Key to the native broadleaf trees of Montana

Key written for dimoose from the Montana Field Guide (Montana Natural Heritage Program and Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks), USDA PLANTS and Virginia Tech Dendrology. Photos from Wikimedia Commons; authors and licenses in the package's COPYRIGHTS file.

    Map of the key11 taxa

    You are here Your path Still possible

    Leaf type? Couplet 1

    • aLeaves compound, divided into separate leaflets.→ 2
    • bLeaves simple, a single blade.→ 3

    Leaflets? Couplet 2 from 1a

    • aLeaves opposite, with 3 (rarely 5) leaflets that have a few coarse teeth or shallow lobes.→ Box elder (Acer negundo)
    • bLeaves opposite, with 5 to 7 leaflets with toothed margins.→ Green ash (Fraxinus pennsylvanica)

    Leaf arrangement? Couplet 3 from 1b

    • aLeaves opposite, with 3 to 5 toothed lobes and red leaf stalks.→ Rocky Mountain maple (Acer glabrum)
    • bLeaves alternate.→ 4

    Leaf lobes? Couplet 4 from 3b

    • aLeaves deeply lobed, the lobes rounded; fruit an acorn.→ Bur oak (Quercus macrocarpa)
    • bLeaves not lobed.→ 5

    Leaf shape? Couplet 5 from 4b

    • aLeaves narrowly lance-shaped, at least 2.5 times as long as wide.→ 6
    • bLeaves broader: rounded, triangular or broadly lance-shaped.→ 7

    Buds? Couplet 6 from 5a

    • aBuds small and pressed against the twig, each covered by a single cap-like scale; leaves 3 to 8 cm long, whitish beneath.→ Peachleaf willow (Salix amygdaloides)
    • bBuds long (about 2.5 cm), curved, resinous and fragrant; leaves 4 to 11 cm long.→ Narrowleaf cottonwood (Populus angustifolia)

    Leaf stalk? Couplet 7 from 5b

    • aLeaf stalks flattened from side to side.→ 8
    • bLeaf stalks round, or only slightly flattened.→ 9

    Leaf shape and teeth? Couplet 8 from 7a

    • aLeaves nearly round, 2 to 8 cm long, finely toothed; bark smooth and pale.→ Quaking aspen (Populus tremuloides)
    • bLeaves triangular, about as long as wide, with teeth at least 1 mm deep.→ Plains cottonwood (Populus deltoides)

    Leaf size? Couplet 9 from 7b

    • aLeaves 5 to 15 cm long, silvery white beneath with rusty smears of resin.→ Black cottonwood (Populus trichocarpa)
    • bLeaves 2 to 7 cm long, with sharp teeth, not silvery white beneath.→ 10

    Bark? Couplet 10 from 9b

    • aBark white and peeling on older trees.→ Paper birch (Betula papyrifera)
    • bBark gray to brown, only slightly peeling; a small tree or large shrub along streams.→ Water birch (Betula occidentalis)
